name: Rahab
charge: Receiving the spies with peace, and believing that the Lord had given Israel the land
summary: A harlot of Jericho, a Canaanite in a city under the ban, hid two spies under the flax on her roof and confessed what the report had done to the whole city: their hearts had melted, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is God in heaven above and in earth beneath. Faith and fear go hand in hand; what she feared was not the king of Jericho but the judgment of the God of this people, and that fear gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She bound the scarlet line in the window, her house alone stood when the wall fell, and she is in the line of Christ.
offenseFull: Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there (Joshua 2:1). When the king of Jericho sent to bring them out, she had already taken the two men and hidden them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there; she told the king’s men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest, saying the men had gone out about the time of the shutting of the gate and urging a quick pursuit (Joshua 2:2-7). The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance. A heathen woman looked out for Israel.

Her faith came by report before it came by sight: she knew the Lord had given them the land, that the terror of Israel had fallen on the city, and that its inhabitants fainted because of them, for they had heard how the Lord dried up the Red sea and what Israel did to Sihon and Og, and as soon as they heard it their hearts melted and no courage remained in any man, because the Lord God of Israel is God in heaven above and in earth beneath (Joshua 2:8-11). That is faith and belief, a heathen acknowledging that the God of Israel had ordained this people to conquer her land, and it is the word of the Most High fulfilled: that day He would begin to put the dread and the fear of Israel on the nations who heard the report (Deuteronomy 2:25).

Faith and fear go hand in hand. She knew the Lord is not to be played with where this people is concerned, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line; she might be caught by her own king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them. It is the same spirit as the woman of Canaan who answered that the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table, and was told that her faith was great (Matthew 15:27-28). She asked them to swear to her by the Lord, since she had shown them kindness, that they would show kindness to her father’s house and save her father, mother, brethren and sisters alive; and the men answered with their own lives for hers, on the condition that she kept their business quiet (Joshua 2:12-14). Rahab the harlot was justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way (James 2:25), and works in the Bible’s own dictionary is keeping His commandments (Psalms 78:7), for the Lord is a God of knowledge and by Him actions are weighed (1 Samuel 2:3).
judgmentFull: The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was on the town wall; anyone who went out of her doors into the street would answer for himself, and anyone who stayed in the house would be Israel’s charge, and she bound the scarlet line in the window (Joshua 2:17-21). The spies hid three days in the mountain until the pursuers turned back, then came to Joshua and reported that the Lord had delivered the whole land into their hands, because all the inhabitants of the country fainted because of them (Joshua 2:22-24).

When the wall fell down flat, her house stood, and Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot’s house to bring out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brethren and all that she had, as they had sworn to her, while everything else in the city was devoted; Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father’s household, and she dwelt in Israel from then on, because she hid the messengers (Joshua 6:22-25). A Canaanite and a heathen was blessed, because she did it to benefit Israel, and that is still the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not welfare and not reparations, but telling this people who they are and that they must keep the commandments of the Most High. By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who did not believe, because she had received the spies in peace (Hebrews 11:31), and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, so the woman spared from the ban stands in the line of David and of Christ (Matthew 1:5). Set beside her is Achan, an Israelite of Judah, who lacked faith and was put to death while the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for hers.

text.text: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot’s house, named Rahab, and lodged there.
And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country.
And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country.
And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were:
And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them.
But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.
And the men pursued after them the way to Jordan unto the fords: and as soon as they which pursued after them were gone out, they shut the gate.
And before they were laid down, she came up unto them upon the roof;
And she said unto the men, I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.

And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.

This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.
And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.
Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.
Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father’s house, and give me a true token:
And that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death.
And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. And it shall be, when the Lord hath given us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with thee.
Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments:
Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
And the men said unto her, We will be blameless of this thine oath which thou hast made us swear.

Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father’s household, home unto thee.

And it shall be, that whosoever shall go out of the doors of thy house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head, and we will be guiltless: and whosoever shall be with thee in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand be upon him.
And if thou utter this our business, then we will be quit of thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.
And she said, According unto your words, so be it. And she sent them away, and they departed: and she bound the scarlet line in the window.
And they went, and came unto the mountain, and abode there three days, until the pursuers were returned: and the pursuers sought them throughout all the way, but found them not.
So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain, and passed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and told him all things that befell them:
And they said unto Joshua, Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us.
But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot’s house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her.

And the young men that were spies went in, and brought out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and all that she had; and they brought out all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel.
And they burnt the city with fire, and all that was therein: only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord.

And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;
